tool.name: CpG Harmonisation: Combine Arrays
tool.description: Merges two array platforms (e.g. 450K + EPIC) into one GenomicRatioSet before cross-platform normalisation

configfiles.configfile:
require('minfi', quietly = TRUE) options(warn = -1)
## minfi::read.metharray() (used by Stage 1) can only parse IDATs from a ## single, homogeneous array type/size in one call - "Trying to parse ## different IDAT files, of different size and type" is what it raises ## if you hand it a mix of e.g. 450K and EPIC samples together. The fix ## is to run Stage 1 (Noob) separately per platform batch first, then ## merge the two resulting GenomicRatioSets here via minfi::combineArrays, ## which aligns them on shared genomic ranges and cbinds the samples ## together - before continuing into Stage 2 (betaqn) on the combined set.
e1 <- new.env() load('$grset_in_1', envir = e1) if (exists('GRSet', envir = e1)) { GRSet1 <- get('GRSet', envir = e1) } else if (exists('GRSet.common', envir = e1)) { GRSet1 <- get('GRSet.common', envir = e1) } else { stop("grset_in_1 .rda must contain an object named 'GRSet' or 'GRSet.common'") }
e2 <- new.env() load('$grset_in_2', envir = e2) if (exists('GRSet', envir = e2)) { GRSet2 <- get('GRSet', envir = e2) } else if (exists('GRSet.common', envir = e2)) { GRSet2 <- get('GRSet.common', envir = e2) } else { stop("grset_in_2 .rda must contain an object named 'GRSet' or 'GRSet.common'") }
platform1.probes <- nrow(GRSet1) platform1.samples <- ncol(GRSet1) platform2.probes <- nrow(GRSet2) platform2.samples <- ncol(GRSet2)
## combineArrays' internal colData merge hits a real bug ("unable to ## find an inherited method for function 'colData<-' for signature ## GenomicRatioSet, AsIs") when both inputs have completely empty ## colData (0 columns) - which is exactly the state Stage 1's output ## is in, since it never sets any pData. Giving each object one real ## column first avoids the degenerate empty-data-frame merge that ## triggers it. pData(GRSet1)\$Platform <- 'platform1' pData(GRSet2)\$Platform <- 'platform2' GRSet <- combineArrays(GRSet1, GRSet2) #aligns on shared genomic ranges, cbinds samples
summary.df <- data.frame( stage = c('platform1_probes', 'platform1_samples', 'platform2_probes', 'platform2_samples', 'combined_probes', 'combined_samples'), count = c(platform1.probes, platform1.samples, platform2.probes, platform2.samples, nrow(GRSet), ncol(GRSet)) ) write.table(summary.df, file = '$summarytab', quote = FALSE, sep = '\t', row.names = FALSE)
save(GRSet, file = '$grset_out')

param.name: grset_in_1
param.label: Platform 1 GenomicRatioSet
param.help: Must contain an object named GRSet - the Stage 1 (Noob background correction) output, run on this platform's IDATs only (e.g. all 450K samples).

param.name: grset_in_2
param.label: Platform 2 GenomicRatioSet
param.help: Must contain an object named GRSet - the Stage 1 (Noob background correction) output, run separately on the other platform's IDATs (e.g. all EPIC samples).

tool.help:
.. class:: infomark
**What it does**
Merges two array-platform batches (e.g. 450K and EPIC) into a single ``GenomicRatioSet`` using ``minfi::combineArrays``, so a mixed-platform study can proceed through the rest of the cross-array harmonisation pipeline (betaqn normalisation, ComBat batch correction, common-probe restriction) as one combined dataset.
**Why this step exists**
``minfi::read.metharray`` (used internally by Stage 1: Noob Background Correction) can only parse IDAT files from a single, homogeneous array type in one call - feeding it a mix of platforms fails with ``[read.metharray] Trying to parse different IDAT files, of different size and type``. The fix is to run Stage 1 *separately* on each platform's IDATs first (producing one Noob-corrected ``GenomicRatioSet`` per platform), then use this tool to merge the two into one combined set before continuing to Stage 2.
``combineArrays`` aligns the two inputs on their shared genomic ranges (not just probe ID strings, so it's robust to platform-specific probe naming/annotation differences) and concatenates the samples together as columns.
***Inputs***
*Platform 1 / Platform 2 GenomicRatioSet*: the Stage 1 output run independently on each platform's raw IDATs (e.g. one run over all 450K samples, one run over all EPIC samples).
***Outputs***
*Combined GenomicRatioSet*: an ``.rda`` file containing the merged ``GRSet``, ready for Stage 2 (Cross-Platform Quantile Normalisation).
*Combine Arrays Summary*: probe and sample counts for each input platform and the combined result, so you can sanity-check that samples weren't dropped unexpectedly.
